text: Open with the outcome. DayShape helps people use free time in ways that feel meaningful, without turning planning into work.
DAYSHAPE

text:
Free time creates a
decision problem
textPreview: Free time creates a | decision problem

text: When the day opens up, people still need to answer three personal questions:
textPreview: When the day opens up, people still need to answer three personal questions:

text:
What do I actually want?
What do I have energy for?
What can fit today?
textPreview: What do I actually want? | What do I have energy for? | What can fit today?

text: A calendar can show an empty slot. It cannot tell you how to spend it.
textPreview: A calendar can show an empty slot. It cannot tell you how to spend it.

text: Most planning tools stop at availability. An empty evening is not the same as a clear decision. DayShape starts with what the person needs right now.
DAYSHAPE
textPreview: DAYSHAPE

text:
The mood map makes
preferences visible
textPreview: The mood map makes | preferences visible

text: Each icon sits on two simple axes: how much the person wants it and how much capacity they have for it.
textPreview: Each icon sits on two simple axes: how much the person wants it and how much capacity they have for it.

text: In the demo, Focus, Novelty, Connection, and Movement all move. The selected icon updates the explanation beside it.
textPreview: In the demo, Focus, Novelty, Connection, and Movement all move. The selected icon updates the explanation beside it.

text: This is the core interaction. It avoids a long questionnaire and gives users a direct way to describe their current state. Mention the two axes: want and capacity.
